title: Finite scalar counit transport through site comparison
statement: For finite commutative rings A,B, a ring map phi, Noetherian schemes X,Y, a compactifiable map f:X->Y and K in intrinsic Dctf(A,Y), assume the ordinary A-exceptional origin of K is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude and the ordinary B-exceptional origin of proScalar(phi)(K) is bounded below. Then the actual pro exceptional coefficient map has the counit identity with the specified proCompactCoefficientInverse [def-pur-finite-smooth-coefficient-arrows] and the original proCounit [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-maps]. Neither smoothness nor an orientation nor invertibility of the exceptional map is assumed.

source.place: Finite scalar counit transport through site comparison; the two-level argument.

proof.text: Put J=origin_A(K), M=f_A^times(J). Finite Tor puts scalar M in the bounded-below locus. The comparison unit at M and counit at comparison(M) are inverse. Expand proCompactCoefficientMap at comparison(M). Move the units with compactSiteNaturality and cancel them with the origin counits. The result is the composite of scalar A-site comparison, Y-site/scalar comparison, ordinary compact coefficient comparison, inverse B-site comparison and compact image of the inverse X-site/scalar comparison. Every factor is invertible on this domain.

Expand proCoefficientMap and proCounit. The bounded-below B-exceptional hypothesis permits naturality of compactSiteMap on its target. Move the ordinary exceptional mate and originReductionMap through that comparison and the B-exceptional counit. Apply the ordinary mates counit identity. The defining adjunction equation for originReductionMap turns its comparison followed by the B-origin counit into inverse site/scalar comparison followed by scalar A-origin counit. Naturality of the Y-site/scalar comparison now identifies both composites. Cancel the invertible compact coefficient map; its total inverse agrees with the categorical inverse on this locus. This proves precisely the displayed identity without using any purity theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteProCoefficientCounitTransport
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasCompactification f]
    (K : proCategory A Y) (_hK : IsCtf A Y K)
    (hG : DerivedCategory.boundedConstructibleFiniteTor A X
      ((rightDerivedUpperShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).obj ((origin A Y).obj K)))
    (hGB : _root_.DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.plus
      ((rightDerivedUpperShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) f).obj
        ((origin B Y).obj ((proScalar φ Y).obj K)))) :
    (proCompact B f).map (proCoefficientMap φ f K) ≫
        proCounit B f ((proScalar φ Y).obj K) =
      proCompactCoefficientInverse φ f ((exceptional A f).obj K) ≫
        (proScalar φ Y).map (proCounit A f K)
